watches.name: Royal Air Force x Gray 43mm - Steel
watches.description: This is a collaboration between Stirling Timepieces and the Royal Air Force Aircrew Profession Advisors at HQ Air Command. The watches are named after Fg Off Donald Garland VC or Sgt Thomas Gray VC, who were awarded the first Royal Air Force Victoria Crosses of World War 2 for actions during the Battle of France. Garland and Gray failed to return, having successfully led, and pressed home, an attack in their Fairey Battle targeting a critically important bridge to slow the enemy advance on 12 May 1940. The design of the watch reflects the classic features of the Service “6BB” and “6B” Aircrew watches that featured the luminous white triangle and/or 2 dots at the 12 o’clock position. It features detail to make it recognisable as Aircrew, from the discrete STANAG 3109 inverted red triangle, to the yellow and black second hand found on controls and levers. The crown is also embellished with the classic “RAF” logo featured on many badges, including flying badges. Each timepiece will be individually serialized, and your own service number can also be added, ensuring a unique and identifiable mark of authenticity. This meticulous detail reinforces the exclusivity and craftsmanship of the collection, adding a personalized touch to each watch. The serial and service number will be discreetly incorporated on the case back, offering a refined yet distinctive element that further elevates the overall design and value of the timepiece. The watch is delivered in a Stirling branded mini peli case. For every watch sold, £15 will be donated to the RAF Benevolent Fund, supporting the vital work they do for serving and former Royal Air Force personnel. Each order will also include the relevant metal wings, either Mission Aircrew or Pilot, to accompany your timepiece. Due to the inclusion of an official image within this design, it is necessary to obtain a license from the Ministry of Defence (MOD). The MOD reserves the right to decline a license if the design does not comply with their guidelines. In the unlikely event that this may occur, a new design will be developed collaboratively between Stirling Timepieces and the project lead. All individuals involved will be promptly informed in such a case. Please note that due to the use of a screw-down case back, the orientation of the Fairey Battle and Gray VC or Garland VC engraving cannot be guaranteed. To ensure a clean, clear print on the dial, the textured finish of the standard Gibson has been replaced with a smooth dial. This product page will close 1st November 2026. Once the product page closes, watches will be delivered between 3 - 5 months after this date.

watches.name: Stirling Tornado x Gibson Chronograph - Steel
watches.description: The Panavia Tornado is the most important European combat aircraft of the Cold War and the years that followed. The aircraft began as the Multi-Role Combat Aircraft (MRCA) and first flew on the 14th August 1974. The 3 nations that built it, Great Britain, Germany and Italy, named the aircraft Tornado. Its swing-wing design made it instantly recognisable and its 2 main variants, the Interdictor Strike (IDS) and Air Defence Variant (ADV), were developed into potent aircraft for Interdiction and Nuclear Strike, Tactical Reconnaissance, Maritime Strike, Electronic Combat and as a long endurance agile Interceptor. These variants were operated with great distinction by the Italian Aeronautica Militare, the German Luftwaffe and Marineflieger, the Royal Saudi Air Force and the Royal Air Force. 990 aircraft were built and some may well still be flying until 2035 some 60 years after the first flight of MRCA. The crews that flew and worked on, and continue to, loved the Tornado and always have immense pride in this special aircraft. Stirling Timepieces are proud to be asked to develop a watch that reflects this incredible aircraft and which allows the Aircrew and Groundcrew to continue this special bond for years to come. Just like the Tornado, the Stirling Tornado comes in 2 main variants: a ‘Diamond Like Carbon’ (DLC) variant in satin black, and ‘Matte Steel’ finished in a low-reflective stainless steel. Both watches resemble the common chronographs worn by Tornado crews at the time (the Seiko Gen 1 and Gen 2 being the most ubiquitous) and are finished with black faces and white luminous detailing. The use of dayglo orange, to mirror the needles and flags used on Tornado flight instruments, and a Tornado aircraft in 67 degree wing with the classic Tornado logo completes the look of the watch face. T he ‘Danger - Explosive Canopy and Seat’ NATO logo common to many Tornado aircraft features on the case back. The crown features an engraved Tornado outline in 25 degree wing. The watches can be engraved with individual Service Numbers on the case back. The Stirling Tornado is a fitting tribute to the many that worked on or flew the Panavia Tornado. It also stands as a reminder of all of those that never returned over the many years that the aircraft flew on operations and training missions across the world. Watches will be produced and assembled once the order window closes on the 31st July 2026, with delivery estimated at 3–5 months from that point. Please note: This timepiece is part of an exclusive limited edition of 150 pieces. Once sold out, no further units will be produced. Due to complex copyright and trademark law, we have only secured the ability to ship this watch to UK and BFPO postal addresses. Panavia GmbH have kindly given their permission to use the TORNADO word-image logo, but we must restrict this to UK and BFPO sales only as another permission already exists within the EU. Any purchases made outside of the UK will be refunded. Due to the use of a screw-down caseback, engraving orientation cannot be guaranteed. To ensure a clean, clear print on the dial, the textured finish of the standard Gibson has been replaced with a smooth dial. While we take great care to match colours as closely as possible to the approved digital render, slight variations between on-screen colours and the final physical product can occasionally occur due to differences in screens, lighting, and production processes.

watches.name: RAF Digby x Burton - Blackout
watches.description: This bespoke Burton Blackout edition has been specially created for current serving members and veterans of RAF Digby. This watch has been designed around the RAF sector clock. The RAF sector clock used in operations at RAF Digby during the Battle of Britain is an iconic 1940’s timepiece with Red, Blue and Yellow 5-minute segments. This enabled commanders to see how "old" a plot was (e.g., a red marker would mean 0- 5 mins old, yellow 5-10 mins) and manage the rapid, ever-changing situation during the Battle of Britain. It allowed fighter controllers to track the age of enemy aircraft sightings by colour, enabling rapid interception decisions to be made by Spitfire pilots. When an aircraft was spotted, the colour under the minute hand was noted, and a corresponding-coloured counter was placed on a plotting table in the control room. The dial features The RAF sector clock markings and a Spitfire aircraft. The caseback shows the unit crest and each watch has been serialised. Watches will be produced and assembled once the order window closes 30th Aug 2026, with delivery estimated at 3–5 months from that point. watches.name: 11th Airborne Division x Durrant - Steel
watches.description: This bespoke edition of the Durrant – Steel has been created exclusively for members of the 11th Airborne Division. Built for professionals who work in some of the most demanding environments on earth, the Durrant combines field-ready durability with understated design. 11th Airborne Division – Pacific Legacy The 11th Airborne Division, known as the “Angels,” earned its reputation during World War II in the Pacific Theater. Activated in 1943, the division trained for airborne and jungle operations before deploying to New Guinea and later the Philippines. Their most notable actions came during the liberation of Luzon in 1945, where they conducted daring airborne assaults, rapid ground advances, and the famous raid on the Los Baños internment camp, rescuing over 2,000 civilians. Operating in harsh terrain against determined resistance, the division proved the effectiveness of vertical envelopment in the Pacific and solidified its place in airborne history. watches.name: Jarvis - Arctic White
watches.description: Forged for operations, The Jarvis is a tactical 42mm GMT dive watch built to perform in the harshest environments. Designed, developed, and tested alongside serving soldiers, this timepiece combines military functionality with rugged durability. Powered by the trusted NH34 automatic movement, The Jarvis delivers accurate multi-time zone tracking, essential for military personnel and contractors operating across borders. The dial, inspired by the explosive det cord found in any breachers kit, features distinctive rings, a nod to its roots in military design. Equipped with a count-up dive bezel and protected by scratch-resistant sapphire crystal, The Jarvis is built to withstand the toughest conditions. Its 316L stainless steel case and rubber strap ensure resilience without compromising on comfort. With a water resistance rating of up to 300 meters, this watch is ready for any deployment, whether on land or sea.

watches.name: Durrant - Arctic White/Steel
watches.description: The heroic actions of the WW2 commando raids inspired our Durrant watch, where soldiers from British and Commonwealth forces were often sent behind enemy lines under the cover of darkness to destroy key infrastructure. We wanted to create a timepiece that embodied the daring actions of those that went before us. The 42mm DLC coated case encapsulates a dial filled with dark shades and tones that represent the early WW2 night operations. The oversized indices and grey hands are filled with Super-LumiNova which makes the dial clear and easy to read at all hours. The handset is beautifully finished with a crisp red outlining to the seconds hand that allows you to track H-hour with precision. Its casing is complemented by a ceramic dive bezel that acts as a nod to the aquatic operations these raids typically came from. Powered by the reliable and respected NH35 automatic movement, you can be confident that this watch will perform under all climates and conditions. The integrated strap keeps the watch close to the wrist to prevent it snagging on modern day wet suits or clothing, whilst the 316L stainless steel hardware is DLC coated to enhance durability.
